human_tolerance.notes: The article says it 'inhabits woodland, farmland, and open country and has also adapted to parks and gardens in urban areas' and nests in holes in trees, buildings and nest boxes; in Japan it forms noisy urban roosts, so it is an exploiter of built land.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeding lasts March to July, often two clutches, in a tree or building hole.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Forms large communal flocks and roosts outside the breeding season.

vocalizations.description: Loud, monotonous series of harsh creaking notes, described as the species' call; given from a perch by day.
Chuckling chatter of feeding flocks on the ground.
Harsh screech given when a flock is alarmed.

taxonomy.note: The GBIF species match on Spodiopsar cineraceus returns usageKey 6100944, rank SPECIES, status ACCEPTED, order Passeriformes, family Sturnidae, genus Spodiopsar, authorship (Temminck, 1835). The article notes the species was formerly placed in Sturnus.

external.note: gbif_usage_key 6100944 from the GBIF species match; inat_taxon_id 547179 from the iNaturalist taxa API (active, rank species, preferred common name 'White-cheeked Starling'); wikidata Q27075595 from the English Wikipedia page's wikibase item.

range.note: Breeding range covers central and north-east China (CN), Korea (KR, KP), Japan (JP) and south-east Siberia (RU); the article also records it in winter in Taiwan (TW). Country codes are a derivation from that prose.

traits.note: Mass 83 g is the EltonTraits BirdFuncDat BodyMass-Value for Sturnus cineraceus (the synonym this species was formerly placed in); the Japanese article gives 70-100 g, whose midpoint is 85 g, so the two agree. Length 24 cm is the English article's stated length. Locomotion Walk and Fly: starlings walk on the ground (the article describes ground-feeding) and fly. Diet follows EltonTraits (invertebrate 60, vertebrate 10, fruit 30), with the vertebrate share folded into invertebrate to give invertebrate 0.7 and fruit 0.3. Lifespan 4 years is carried from the congener common myna record, both being Sturnidae, and is a judgement. No source states a wingspan, so wingspan_m 0.39 is inferred from the congener common myna record (0.378 m wingspan at 0.23 m length), scaled to this species' 0.24 m length.

habitat.note: The article states it inhabits woodland, farmland and open country and has adapted to parks and gardens, nesting in a hole in a tree, building or nest box, and eating fruit and insects; use is split ground 0.5 / arboreal 0.5, shelter is a cavity, and resources follow the nest hole and diet. human_tolerance is Exploiter from the urban adaptation and communal roosts described in the Japanese article.

seasonal.note: Breeding lasts March to July with often two clutches, and the species forms large communal flocks and roosts outside the breeding season; strategy ActiveYearRound. Juvenile duration 28 days is the upper bound of the sourced 14-15 day incubation plus 13-15 day fledging.

vocalizations.note: The English article describes 'the loud, monotonous call is a series of harsh, creaking notes'; the Japanese article gives 'gyā-gyā', 'gyuru-gyuru' and 'michi-michi'. The three calls are a judgement mapping those onto the program's song, contact and alarm slots.

look.note: The Description gives a dark grey-brown bird with a paler belly, a whitish band across the rump, whitish cheeks and forehead, white tail border, orange legs and an orange bill with a black tip; the Japanese article adds a 60-70 mm tail. Modelled features: the whitish cheek and forehead as a mirrored cheek box, the whitish rump as a rump box, and the orange bill and legs in the accent slot. Proportions and remaining palette are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: food_tag invertebrate follows the insect-rich diet, song and alarm bind the creaking call and the harsh alarm, and nest months bracket the March-July breeding season.
